The accurate distinction is that law as a medium consists of formal, general rules that steer and control the state and the economy, while law as an institution consists of shared norms and values anchored in the lifeworld. Law as a medium is positivized steering law whose legitimacy comes from the legal order as a whole; law as an institution still needs moral-practical justification for particular norms such as constitutional basics and the moral core of criminal law. The alternative that treats “medium” as media presentation and “institution” as the courts does not match Habermas.
CONFIDENCE: 92
